claims.text: Keep a Changelog: changelogs are for humans; latest version first; same types of changes grouped; types Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security; keep an Unreleased section at the top.

Keep a Changelog: using commit log diffs as changelogs is a bad idea (noise); a commit documents a step in the code's evolution, a changelog entry the noteworthy difference, often across multiple commits, for end users.

CHANGELOG.md@stage-2 lines 1-9: intro (readers, newest first, Keep a Changelog, SemVer 2.0.0) and rule 'Each pull request that changes behaviour adds a line under Unreleased'; lines 11-13: empty ## [Unreleased], then ## [1.0.0] - 2026-09-27.

CHANGELOG.md@stage-2 lines 58-66: 1.0.0 ### Removed lists POST /api/v1/auth/login with the Keycloak alternative; ### Fixed lists cancelling a shipped order now answers 409 (already-shipped); line 68 ## [0.1.0] - 2026-09-26.
CHANGELOG.md@stage-2 uses only the headings Added, Changed, Removed, Fixed under versions.

git log --oneline stage-1..stage-2 in examples/don-hang lists 35 commits; none of their subjects contains 'login' (grep -ci login -> 0); the removal is in ba5c998 'auth: Keycloak issues tokens; api checks them, StaffOnly and OrderOwner'.
grep -n 'auth/login' CHANGELOG.md at stage-2 prints lines 60 (Removed, 1.0.0) and 72 (Added, 0.1.0).

claims.text: release.yml@stage-2 does not edit CHANGELOG.md; it reads the version's section (scripts/release-notes.sh), so renaming Unreleased to the version is done by hand before tagging.

Some teams generate changelogs from commit messages in a fixed format (e.g. Conventional Commits with release tools); writing entries by hand per pull request keeps them in the reader's words at the cost of one line per PR.
Đơn Hàng went from version 0.1.0 (commit stage-1) to 1.0.0 (commit stage-2): v0.1.0 is on 75bf7d2, v1.0.0 on 7a131bc.
claims.source_hint: git -C examples/don-hang rev-parse v0.1.0^{commit} stage-1^{commit} v1.0.0^{commit} stage-2^{commit}

claims.text: SemVer 2.0.0: 0.y.z is initial development where anything may change; 1.0.0 defines the public API (CHANGELOG.md@stage-2 line 15: 'The first version with a declared public API'), so 0.1.0 -> 1.0.0 does not by itself say what changed.
The bodies of ba5c998, d617581 and 9c0814f mention the removed POST /api/v1/auth/login; no subject in stage-1..stage-2 does.
In git log A..B, the range lists commits reachable from B but not from A; wc -l counts lines; grep -c counts matching lines, -i ignores case, -n prefixes line numbers.
